{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZkBhEw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhDKrEc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 51, "title": "Implement SCU A-to-B DMA startup ordering against pending SH-2 writes", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `337215d2ba057a29a65fc43d517450618626bb99`, `Bus::allocate_bus_transaction` considers SCU DMA before queued CPU buffered writes. It preserves an already granted physical beat, but has no route-aware distinction between an A-to-B transfer awaiting startup and one already running. An ungranted SH-2 A/B-bus write can consequently remain queued while DMA starts.

This can reverse device-write ordering around CD-to-video or CD-to-sound transfers. Existing buffered-write, DMA beat and preemption tests establish useful mechanisms without validating this startup contract.

## Expected outcome

Implement the documented A-to-B DMA startup interlock through the existing hardware-time transaction scheduler, covering both SH-2 requesters and direct/indirect DMA.

The primary contract is [Sega ST-210-110194, §3, item 12, printed p.5](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-210-110194.pdf): CPU A/B writes take precedence before A/B DMA activation, while CPU A/B accesses wait once the transfer starts. Item 8 warns against software accessing these buses during the transfer; item 1 prohibits DMA writes to A-bus. Therefore the supported transfer direction here is A-to-B. Do not invent B-to-A operation or physical hang behavior.

Use [ST-097-R5, §§2.1, 3.2 and 3.6](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-097-R5-072694.pdf) with applicable final-spec corrections for DMA and bus coordination. Preserve the documented descending DMA-level priority; this Issue does not request reversing it.

Keep startup qualification separate from subsequent transfer beats. Preserve retained operands, separately completed B-bus halfwords, descriptor acquisition, waits, interrupt delivery and reset domains. Restrict the change to this interlock and necessary validation/documentation; do not introduce blanket CPU-before-DMA arbitration.

## Context and reproduction

Planning inspection used the supplied main revision, which matches the clean checkout. No files were changed and no test suite was rerun. The supplied main CI observation is `in_progress`, with no conclusion; it establishes neither success nor failure. No open task Issues were listed in the supplied snapshot.

Relevant implementation:

- `src/bus/transactions.rs:705`: buffered-write admission acknowledges the CPU separately from external publication.
- `src/bus/transactions.rs:926`: SCU DMA selection occurs before the CPU buffered-write branch at line 1027.
- `src/scu/transactions.rs:89`: cycle preparation selects a channel and probes its next operation without considering pending CPU A/B writes.
- `src/scu/dma.rs:154`: direct initialization, descriptor acquisition and transfer progression provide the existing resumable DMA mechanism.

Create a focused native reproduction with a queued, ungranted CPU A/B write and a pending A-to-B transfer at the same arbitration opportunity. Include an already occupied bus so the CPU write is genuinely pending. Inspect actual publication order and source consumption, rather than inferring ordering from final completion alone.

For guest integration, author an original licensed mixed-disc diagnostic that performs a finite SH-2 device-write sequence while a hardware trigger requests CD-FIFO-to-B-bus DMA. An overlapping destination and distinct data patterns should make reversed ordering observable. Execute real guest instructions, CD FIFO reads, DMA writes and an end-interrupt handler. Host code may inspect results but must not supply completion or device effects.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document the corrected hardware contract with exact primary sections, including the meaning of pending startup versus active transfer. Identify any equal-edge or continuous-write boundary convention that the specifications leave unspecified. Evidence-backed corrections to this AI-authored task must be documented in the source Issue without weakening validation or requiring human confirmation.
- [ ] Add independent native transaction vectors proving that qualifying queued CPU writes drain before A-to-B data transfer starts. Cover master and slave requesters, all three DMA levels individually, direct and indirect operation, software start and a hardware trigger, and representative VDP1, VDP2 and sound-memory destinations. Derive expected ordering before running the implementation.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the new ordering assertion fails against the inherited arbiter. Check source-read counts, individual destination publications and absence of premature DMA-end IRQ; comparing final copied bytes alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Verify startup continuity and isolation: finite continued CPU writes defer activation; ending the sequence permits bounded progress; a running transfer is not repeatedly treated as a fresh startup. Preserve unrelated-route arbitration, valid DMA-level preemption, descriptor reads, retained halfwords and the existing single queued retrigger. Do not impose guaranteed ordering for prohibited three-channel concurrency.
- [ ] Test cancellation during pending startup and active data phases using the applicable reset domains. Preserve completed effects, cancel unfinished work appropriately, and prove that no stale source read, destination write or interrupt appears after cancellation. Verify repeatability across advancement chunks such as 1/3/17/10000 and with passive debugger inspection.
- [ ] Add the reproducible original guest/media fixture to native integration and the existing production Wasm/headless-browser suite under `/saturn-rust/`. Assert guest-computed records, exact source consumption, DMA results and real handler execution. Include changed source/write operands, an omitted-trigger control, repeated cold boots and at least one observable rendered result from the transferred video data. Derive expectations independently of production arbitration helpers.
- [ ] Preserve existing tests and demonstrations, including buffered writes, TAS, refresh, direct/indirect DMA, byte fringes, preemption, DSP transfers, CD FIFO replay, Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab. Revise an inherited expectation only with an explicit primary-reference justification; retain its original regression purpose.
- [ ] Update the conformance matrix and an Issue-specific validation record with implementation/test links, actual results, conventions and remaining limitations. Run the repository-required formatting, locked build/test, native/Wasm Clippy, web build, fixture/media reproducibility and complete browser checks without skipping required coverage.

This is a partial #17 increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral, multiprocessor/bus/reset, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration requirements remain mandatory. Administrative closure and green CI do not establish hardware completion. Genuine BIOS and broad commercial-game compatibility remain unverified. Do not reopen historical trackers or use closing keywords for #17.

## Optional validation

Additional deterministic bus traces may help diagnose ordering. Personal firmware, commercial media, physical hardware, human approval and live Pages inspection are not required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
